title: Understanding Trap Seals in Drainage Systems
description: Every plumbing fixture connected to a drainage system relies on a water trap to prevent hazardous sewer gases from entering living spaces. Maintaining this protective water barrier is a fundamental principle of sanitary drainage design. If a fixture goes unused for an extended period, the water inside the trap can evaporate, allowing sewer odors to leak into the building. Professional plumbers always check trap seals during maintenance calls and understand how proper venting prevents siphonage from pulling the water barrier out of the trap entirely.

Understanding Trap Seals in Drainage Systems

Every plumbing fixture connected to a drainage system relies on a water trap to prevent hazardous sewer gases from entering living spaces. Maintaining this protective water barrier is a fundamental principle of sanitary drainage design. If a fixture goes unused for an extended period, the water inside the trap can evaporate, allowing sewer odors to leak into the building. Professional plumbers always check trap seals during maintenance calls and understand how proper venting prevents siphonage from pulling the water barrier out of the trap entirely.
